tier_reason: B stands: independent measurement; the baseline is fair for the usual non-LTO HAL build, though the README misexplains the gap.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: the README blames the HAL gap on parameter checks and says HAL is inlined at -O2; both are wrong: USE_FULL_ASSERT is off (assert_param is ((void)0U)), LTO is off, and the F0 HAL_GPIO_WritePin is a branch plus one BSRR/BRR store called out of line, so the measured gap is call overhead only. Each row is a hand-edited build (the committed main.c has the HAL block on), with no build logs or disassembly. The benchmark repo has no licence: cite the numbers, do not copy its code. The book's own code uses BSRR |= (a needless read), ODR ^= (not interrupt-safe) and empty for-loop delays.

tier_reason: C to D: LL_GPIO_SetOutputPin/ResetOutputPin are static inline single BSRR (F3: BRR) stores, the same instruction as the direct-register loop, yet LL measured 1.09/1.18 MHz against 2.94/5.54-6.00 MHz for the register loop, so the LL calls were not inlined: an unoptimised build at an unstated -O level. The only numeric win (about 1.35x over HAL) is a Debug-build artifact, not LL speed (-O0 downgrade precedent; no valid measurement).

corrections.claimed_speedup: No valid numeric win: the tutorial's LL set/reset rate (1.09 MHz) against HAL_GPIO_WritePin (806 kHz), about 1.35x (derived from page data), comes from an unoptimised build in which the static inline LL functions were not inlined; optimised, LL compiles to the same single store as direct register access. Toggle rates were equal (625 kHz).
corrections.caveats: Enricher: the same direct-register code ran at 5.54 vs 6.00 MHz across the two projects, showing build drift; measured on STM32F3 parts (F334R8, F334C8), not the F4 driver; the tutorial has no licence.
